title: Unveiling Therapeutic Targets for Precision Intervention in HPV-Associated Oral Cancers through Genomic Analysis
text:
This project aims to analyze TCGA data to investigate the role of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in HPV-
positive head and neck cancers, focusing on the impact of viral integration on cancer progression and gene
regulation.

title: Regulation of Adherent Cell Proliferation by Matrix Viscoelasticity
text:
Extracellular matrix stiffness and viscoelasticity regulates cell proliferation in 3D microenvironments through
mechanotransduction, but the mechanisms mediating these effects remain largely unclear. Here we will combine
biophysical approaches with genome-wide analyses and CRISPR screens to determine the mechanisms
mediating the impact of matrix stiffness and viscoelasticity on cell proliferation. Therefore, the proposed research
is relevant to the part of NIH’s mission that seeks to develop fundamental knowledge that will help reduce the
burdens of human disability and disease.

title: Gene editing in the brain with CRISPR-PEG
text:
The experiments in this proposal focus on developing a new Cas9 delivery vehicle termed CRISPR-PEG.
CRISPR-PEG is designed to edit large volumes of brain tissue and in this proposal we will use it to treat mouse
models of fragile X syndrome and related disorders. If successful, the experiments in this proposal will develop
a new strategy for treating genetic disorders.

title: Next-Generation Oncoproteomic Sequencing and Precision Profiling
text:
The proposed technology will deliver ultra-precise, high-throughput sequencing and profiling of both cancer-
related proteins and general proteomes, identifying critical mutations and post-translational modifications with
unprecedented accuracy. This platform has strong commercial potential for broader applications in
biotechnology, diagnostics, and personalized medicine, facilitating earlier disease detection, targeted therapies,
and comprehensive protein analysis. Improving protein characterization and oncoprotein identification will
directly advance public health and reduce healthcare costs.

title: "A PHASE I STUDY INVESTIGATING THE SAFETY & EFFICACY OF DANVATIRSEN AS MONOTHERAPY FOLLOWED BY COMBINATION WITH VENETOCLAX IN PATIENTS WITH RELAPSED/REFRACTORY MDS & AML."
text:
Aggressive myeloid malignancies such as high-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) and
acute myeloid leukemia (AML) are difficult to treat and frequently not cured by conventional
chemotherapy. Relapsed/refractory (R/R) MDS/AML have a very poor prognosis. Through the
means of this proposal, we will conduct an early phase clinical trial of a novel antisense STAT3
inhibitor in patients with R/R MDS/AML and also investigate ways to overcome therapy
resistance in MDS/AML.

title: Fast-Track Phage-amplified MALDI-TOF MS for rapid phenotypic UTI diagnosis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing
text:
Cobio NIH SBIR Fast-Track Project Narrative
Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are the most common infection type in the U.S., and life-threatening antibiotic
resistance in these infections is increasing at an alarming rate. Current UTI diagnostics rely on time-consuming
pre-analysis organism isolation and enrichment that requires an average of 1-3 days and do not provide
comprehensive antibiotic susceptibility data to inform drug selection. The goal of this SBIR Fast-Track project
is to address these key drawbacks by demonstrating the effectiveness of PhAAST-MALDI, which is Cobio
Diagnostics’ proprietary phage-amplified MALDI-TOF MS (matrix-assisted laser-desorption ionization time-of-
flight mass spectrometry) direct-from-specimen assay for bacterial ID, AST and MIC in urine.

title: Regulation of neurodevelopmental cell behaviors in Ciona
text:
Human development depends greatly on the shaping and movements of individual cells. Congenital
syndromes, cancer, and other cell diseases occur when there is a breakdown in the regulation of the
behaviors of specific cells. We will use the small, transparent embryos of Ciona, one of the
invertebrates most closely related to humans, to better understand which genes are activated to
regulate such behaviors during neural development, and how cell behavior goes awry when these
genes are missing or defective.

title: Identifying Endocrine-Disrupting Plastic Additives using Machine Learning
text:
Plastic additives are widely used chemicals, some of which are known to cause adverse health effects - yet
thousands of plastic additives remain uncharacterized for their risk of disrupting endocrine function via AR and
ERα modulation. Here, we will develop an integrated computational (Aim 1) and experimental (Aim 2) workflow
to systematically predict and validate the AR and ERα modulating and endocrine-disrupting potential of plastic
additives. This platform will provide critical public health data on the adverse effects of plastic additives and serve
as a blueprint for future machine learning-assisted toxicology research into commonly used materials and
important toxicological endpoints.

title: Identification of botanical hHv1 channel blockers as analgesics for neuropathic pain
text:
This research addresses a specific unmet medical need, the absence of effective therapeutics for neuropathic
pain (NeuP), a debilitating chronic pain syndrome that develops as a result of nerve injuries caused by trauma
or disease and affects over 16 million Americans. This proposal seeks to optimize a novel fluorescent high-
throughput screening (HTS) assay for identifying small molecule blockers of the voltage-gated proton channel
(Hv1) from botanicals that reduce the release of inflammatory mediators by microglia and thereby relieve NeuP.
The project will build on preliminary findings to optimize the HTS assay and identify lead compounds for devel-
opment as drugs targeting Hv1; these agents will have a number of other potential uses because Hv1 is central
not only to the development of NeuP but also contributes to tissue damage after ischemic stroke and spinal cord
injury.

title: Neurophysiology of impaired gait in mouse models of Parkinson’s disease
text:
Impairments in limb movements during walking, or gait, are a debilitating motor symptom of Parkinson’s disease
for which no fully effective treatment exists. The neural circuit mechanisms that cause these gait disturbances
have not been well studied at the resolution of individual limb movements. Therefore, the goal of this project is
to understand how gait-related brain activity is altered in animal models of Parkinson's disease.

title: Genetic Dissection of Germ Cell Differentiation and Function
text:
Understanding the unique mechanisms that govern germ cell formation and function will have a
positive impact on medical science. We seek to gain new insights into the molecules that control
germ cell differentiation and how germ cells protect the integrity of their genomes.

title: Pacific Island Partnerships for Cancer Health for Everyone (PIPCHE)
text:
OVERALL
The Pacific Island Partnership for Cancer Health for Everyone (PIPCHE) represents the next step in augmenting a Hawai‘i-Guam-USAPI cancer research infrastructure by investing in Pacific Island Populations leaders, Early Stage Investigators, community partners, and community-research. As a result of the 22-year commitment, PIPCHE is also well positioned to increase the biomedical cancer science workforce and research leadership that better reflects the Hawai‘i-Guam-USAPI population and to stimulate new areas of cancer research. PIPCHE has assembled dedicated academic and community partnerships needed to synergistically accelerate cancer research into a sustainable forum that pursues cultural and environmental appropriate solutions.

title: Structure and function of Transient Receptor Potential Channels
text:
Transient Receptor Potential (TRP) channels are regulated by a broad range of stimuli, including chemicals,
temperature and mechanical stress and are directly involved in sensory perception such as taste, olfaction,
thermal perception and nociception. TRP channels are implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous diseases
and some of them represent important prognostic markers and promising targets for new therapeutic strategies
to treat a variety of human cancers. Our goal is to study TRP channels using a combination of biophysical and
biochemical techniques and to obtain detailed information about their structure and function that will help to
develop new drug design strategies.

title: Perfused organ panel as an animal surrogate for chemical toxicity testing
text:
This project will lay out foundation for new, alternative, animal-relevant test systems for sensitive, reliable and
predictive in vitro testing of environmental toxicants, such as organophosphate and carbamate pesticides, to
ethically and humanely identify potential hazards to human health and the environment.

title: Harnessing big data to understand the confluence of HIV and cancer stigma in the US Southeast
text: Although stigma is a major barrier to care that impacts people living with the dual burden of HIV and cancer in the US, little is known about the causal mechanisms through which stigma impacts cancer care delivery and long-term survivorship care to manage both HIV and living as a cancer survivor. We aim to address this gap in scientific knowledge, leveraging a novel electronic health record-based linkage of multiple health systems throughout Florida called OneFlorida+ (>24 million patients) to gain real-world insights into (1) patterns and trends in cancer treatment, cancer survivorship care, and HIV care after a cancer diagnosis; (2) negative impacts of stigma on care behaviors among PWH with cancer to identify actionable targets for intervention; and (3) gain insights from PWH with cancer served by community-based clinics and an NCI-designated cancer center through qualitative interviews to understand the impacts of stigma within two care contexts. Our results will elucidate mechanisms to inform the development of future interventions to: 1) address the impacts of stigma on care delivery to PWH, 2) improve coverage of cancer and survivorship care among PWH, and 3) optimize care guidelines for PWH.

title: Mitochondrial Membrane Dynamics in Th17 Cells
text: Certain types of T cells can promote inflammation and autoimmunity, while others can suppress immune responses. This proposal’s objective is to understand how changes in mitochondria, the so-called powerhouses of the cell, impact the function of different types of T cells. Defining the mechanisms that regulate T cell metabolism will be critical for gaining new insights into how to therapeutically target these cells in the context of autoimmunity, infection, and inflammatory diseases.

title: Biostatistics Training Program in Cancer Research
text:
The need for rigorously trained statistical scientists and data scientists in cancer research is
massive and continues to increase. In addition to advanced coursework in biostatistics and
epidemiology the interdisciplinary training program will give trainees who are obtaining a Ph.D. in
Biostatistics or Epidemiology (i) a solid understanding of cancer biology, (ii) experience and ability
to communicate and collaborate with cancer scientists, (iii) understanding of recent developments
in cancer requiring innovative statistical research and (iv) independent research skills. The aim
of the University of Michigan Cancer Biostatistics Training Program (CBTP) is to increase the
participation in cancer research of the new generation of biostatisticians who are educated not
only in the powerful methods of modern statistics and data science, but also in the biology and
epidemiology of cancer, the current body of knowledge about the etiology of the disease, its
prevention, detection, natural history, and treatment.

title: Girk3 in bone biology and disease
text:
Osteoporosis is a prevalent disease characterized by low bone mineral density, bone fragility, and fractures.
Mice lacking the potassium ion channel Girk3 have elevated bone mass and reduced circulating cytokines in
adulthood, making Girk3 a novel target for bone remodeling. This research will determine the physiological and
cellular mechanisms by which Girk3 regulates cytokine production and bone mass and test whether Girk3
deletion prevents ovariectomy-induced osteoporosis in a cytokine-dependent manner.

title: PowerEdge XE9680, a NVIDIA H200-powered AI Server
text:
An NVIDIA H200-powered AI server can accelerate cancer research and improve patient outcomes. This
advanced infrastructure will enable real-time analysis of complex biomedical data, including genomics, imaging,
and clinical records, supporting the development of predictive models for treatment response, toxicity, and
disease progression. By powering AI-driven tools for biomarker discovery, clinical trial optimization, and
personalized therapy, the server will help clinicians make faster, more accurate decisions tailored to each patient;
this investment directly supports our mission to lead in precision oncology and deliver more effective, data-
informed care.

title: Molecular Genetics Core
text: The overall goal of this Core is to support and advance diabetes-related research through the generation of unique, genetically-modified mutant mouse models. We currently provide a number of highly specialized services contained within two tightly integrated Subcores: 1) the Molecular Subcore designs and generates gene expression constructs and CRISPR tools for genetic modification in mice and cultured cell lines, provides genotyping design/ mutation characterization, gene mapping/ localization and the quantitation of gene expression by quantitative RT-PCR, and 2) the Gene Targeting Subcore generates genetically-modified mouse models in a variety of standard strains (such as C57BL/6, Balb/c, etc.) and specialized genetic backgrounds (including NOD and various immunodeficient strains, such as Rag/Il2rg KOs) via CRISPR/Cas9 approaches, conventional transgenesis and ES cell recombination methods, and also provides sperm cryopreservation and IVF recovery of preserved strains. The specific aims of the Molecular Genetic Mouse Core are therefore to provide the following: a) critical services, b) technical assistance, c) experimental design, consultation/ advice, troubleshooting, d) training and e) equipment and resources, centered around the generation of genetically- modified mouse models by a variety of both traditional and CRISPR-related methods, including knock-outs, conditional knockouts, inducible knockouts, conditional gene activation, and a variety of knock-ins (tags, reporters, mutations and exon/domain or whole gene replacements). The MGM Core has successfully generated a great many lines of genetically-modified mice related to diabetes studies, most recently using CRISPR-based technology, and its continuing focus on technological development will ensure that services to the diabetes community remain cutting-edge. In addition, a unique feature of this core is that the interests of the subcore directors have fueled a critical mass of resources for investigation of the rapidly developing research areas of the mechanistic relationships between gut microbiota, inflammasome biology and obesity, NAFLD, and type 1 and type 2 diabetes. The MGM Core has developed mouse models with ablated or altered genes involved in regulation of the innate immune system, including NOD-like receptor proteins, Toll-like receptors, guanylate binding proteins, the apolipoprotein L family, and various interleukins and caspases. Finally, the core has a continuing investment in extending and improving the development and application of technologies for humanization of the mouse genome for engraftment of CD34+ human HSC, and the reconstitution of a human hematopoietic and immune system. These “humanized” mouse models will be invaluable tools for the dissection of the genetic components regulating the immunologic and metabolic responses in both type 1 and type 2 diabetes, especially with respect to human disease.
